report:
## Conclusion: No, hydroxychloroquine does not reduce COVID-19 mortality

The weight of high-quality evidence confirms your instinct. Large, well-conducted randomized controlled trials consistently show hydroxychloroquine provides **no mortality benefit** for COVID-19 patients, and in some cases raises safety concerns.

**Key evidence:**

1. **RECOVERY Trial (UK)** – One of the largest COVID-19 treatment trials (>11,000 hospitalized patients), it found "no significant difference in mortality rate at 28 days between those randomised to hydroxychloroquine treatment and those to usual care." Results were also published in NEJM (https://www.nejm.org/doi/full/10.1056/NEJMoa2016638). Source: https://www.recoverytrial.net/results/hydroxychloroquine-results and https://pharmaceutical-journal.com/article/news/recovery-trial-to-stop-enrolling-patients-to-ineffective-hydroxychloroquine-arm

2. **WHO Solidarity Trial** – A multinational RCT that, combined with France's Discovery trial data, showed hydroxychloroquine "does not result in the reduction of mortality of hospitalised COVID-19 patients, when compared with standard of care." This led WHO to halt the hydroxychloroquine arm. Source: https://www.who.int/news-room/questions-and-answers/item/coronavirus-disease-covid-19-hydroxychloroquine

3. **Cochrane Systematic Review** – This independent, rigorous meta-analysis of randomized trials concluded that hydroxychloroquine has "little or no effect on the risk of death" and likely no effect on progression to mechanical ventilation. Source: https://www.cochrane.org/fr/CD013587/INFECTN_la-chloroquine-ou-lhydroxychloroquine-est-elle-utile-pour-traiter-les-personnes-atteintes-de-la

**Note on conflicting claims:** Some websites and blogs cite observational studies or non-peer-reviewed "meta-analyses" (e.g., aggregator sites) claiming benefit, but these are generally lower-quality, non-randomized, or methodologically compromised compared to the RCTs above. Major health authorities (WHO, NIH, FDA) do not recommend hydroxychloroquine for COVID-19 treatment based on this trial evidence.

**Bottom line:** Multiple large RCTs and a Cochrane meta-analysis—the gold standards of medical evidence—confirm hydroxychloroquine does not reduce COVID-19 mortality.
